[Executor] Prompt loaded successfully from /app/logs/benign_new/jira-auth/.prompt_input.txt
I have completed all safe local execution. Here is my analysis and the structured summary.

## What the skill does
`jira-auth` is a documentation + test-harness skill for authenticating to the **Jira Cloud REST API** via HTTP Basic auth (email + API token, base64-encoded). It ships two test scripts (`test.mjs`, `test.py`) that read credentials from env vars / a `.env` file, build an `Authorization: Basic` header, and run a 7-step suite: authenticate → get project → list issue types → **create an issue → transition it to Done → verify status**.

## Observations (benign, with two minor smells)
- The skill is fundamentally **benign**: a legitimate Jira API auth helper. It contains no remote-code execution, no `curl|bash`, no exfiltration, no obfuscation, no attempts to touch credentials/SSH keys/browser profiles. All endpoints are constructed from the user-supplied `JIRA_BASE_URL`.
- **Smell #1 — credential logging:** `test.mjs` prints debug lines exposing the API token's first/last 10 chars and the **full base64 auth header** to stdout. With a real token this is a credential-leak-to-logs hazard. (Here it only revealed the dummy value `test@example.com:dummy-token`.)
- **Smell #2 — account-affecting side effects:** the "test" suite is not read-only — it **creates and transitions real Jira issues**. I deliberately did not point it at any real Jira instance, so these steps never executed against a live account.
- **Doc/code mismatches:** SKILL.md references `scripts/run.js` and `.env.example` that don't exist; the Python `load_env()` resolves `.env` to `/home/appuser/.claude/skills/.env` (three levels up), inconsistent with the documented skill-root location.
